Here, the denominator is the imaginary number $6\text{i}.$ Note that this can be written as $0+6\text{i},$ so the conjugate is $0-6\text{i},$ or simply $-6\text{i}.$

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-6\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9-5\text{i}}{6\text{i}} & =\frac{9-5\text{i}}{6\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-6\text{i}}{-6\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-54\text{i}+30{\text{i}}^{2}}{-36{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-54\text{i}+30(-1)}{-36(-1)} \\  & =\frac{-30-54\text{i}}{36}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-30-54\text{i}}{36} & =-\frac{30}{36}-\frac{54}{36}\text{i} \\  & =(-\frac{5}{6})+(-\frac{3}{2})\,\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
